page: Amazon Web Services d3en.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include an L3 cache of 35 MB, AVX-512 instruction set support, and dedicated CPU allocation. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps.

Storage density is the primary design characteristic of this instance, delivering 55,920 GB of local HDD storage bundled directly with the compute resource. The instance does not feature dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense local HDD capacity positions the server toward large-capacity storage applications rather than high-IOPS transactional tiers.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution for general workloads alongside limitations in compute-heavy execution. The instance scores 1,161.0 on Geekbench single-core and 4,427.0 on multi-core, with a PassMark CPU score of 7,724.51 and PassMark memory score of 2,354.06. Stress-ng single-core performance places in the bottom 25% with a score of 1,326.69, while multi-core achieves an average tier of 6,980.42. Database operations score 2,715.99 in PassMark, and Redis SET throughput measures 6.7 million operations per second. Static web serving reaches 7.17 GB/sec, while larger language model processing shows poor throughput due to the absence of dedicated acceleration.

From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes raw disk capacity per compute core, offering massive storage density relative to its 8-vCPU allocation. Workloads suited for this server include distributed file systems, data lakes, log aggregation, secondary backup tiers, batch ETL processing, and big data architectures requiring broad HDD capacity alongside balanced networking throughput.

Its defining component is 55,920 GB of bundled local HDD storage, offering substantial capacity for density-focused data retention. The system lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show balanced mid-tier results across PassMark (7,724.51 CPU score) and Geekbench (4,427.0 multi-core), with average ratings in memory bandwidth, Redis throughput (6.7 million ops/sec), and static web delivery (7.17 GB/sec), though single-thread compute benchmarks reflect lower-tier performance. The instance is suited for data lake clusters, log aggregation repositories, batch processing, and high-capacity storage workloads.
